subject: Mediation with continuous and binary mediator

messages.author: ac3350bb82db2fde
messages.subject: Mediation with continuous and binary mediator
parts:
Hi, 

I am trying to run a mediation model, with one of the mediators being a binary variable (negative). It resulted in a warning message. I tried then to order the data and it resulted in an error message. I tried using missing='pairwise' but that didn't work for me. All this 'issues' are not presented when I exclude the binary variable ('negative') from the model.   Could I still use the results and the model without ordering the variables so that the 'negative' variable can remain in the model?


model <- '
# outcome model (Direct effect)
Return_MK ~ f*MK.sat_mean + d*negative + b*MK.exp_mean 

#mediator 
MK.exp_mean ~ a*MK.sat_mean
negative ~ c*MK.sat_mean

#indirect effect
sat_neg := c*d
sat_exp := a*b

#mediator correlation
negative ~~ MK.exp_mean
'
MK.exp_mean
fit <- sem(model, data=MK.2.mean, bootstrap=10000)
summary(fit, standardized = TRUE,  fit.measures=TRUE)


1.) 
Warning message:
In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, group.label = group.label,  :
  lavaan WARNING: unordered factor(s) with more than 2 levels detected in data: negative


2.) 
Error in muthen1984(Data = X[[g]], ov.names = ov.names[[g]], ov.types = ov.types,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: some categories of variable `MK.exp_mean' are empty in group 1; frequencies are [1 1 2 3 4 4 5 6 4 2 10 12 7 11 16 11 18 18 14 9 11 7 4 6 23 0]

=============================================================================================

I look for examples online but it seems that the fit.measures result are not always shown in the examples. I ran it anyway and I get 'NAs' for the Loglikelihood and AIC, BIC. Is that because one of the mediators is binary? The estimator is ML and not WLS. I changed it to WLS and it does not show both Loglikelihood and AIC, BIC. So, I just wanted confirmation. 

Loglikelihood and Information Criteria:

  Loglikelihood user model (H0)                     NA

  Number of free parameters                          9

  Bayesian (BIC)                                             NA


=============================================================================================

Lastly, how could I interpret the r-square in the model? I am more interested in the individual variables estimates, but I was wondering if I was missing anything.

Hi, I am not much experienced to give you full support on the issue. However, I experienced somewhat similar error recently. I found that some of the variables where highly correlated (>1). When I modify the model specification, the problem was resolved. Just to give the hint to inspect your model. I also had negative variable but that was not problematic. I hope others can give more technically detail feedback.

Ashenafi
